guideTitle: 6 Best Overbed Tables for Queen Beds in 2026
metaTitle: Best Overbed Tables for Queen Beds in 2026
metaDescription: Six rolling overbed tables sized for queen beds around 70.9 inches long, compared on height range, tilt, power ports, storage and caster brakes.
introParagraphs: A queen mattress is about 60 inches wide, which means a table around 70 inches long can straddle the frame with legs standing on the floor at each side. That span is common across the tables in this guide, and it is why a queen bed is the easiest size to shop for.

We evaluated six tables from their listed specs and from buyer feedback, without claiming hands-on testing. Four of the six share a 70.9 inch length, so the real differences are tilt angles, storage, power outlets and how many wheels lock. One pick, the TigerDad, telescopes so it can also serve a smaller or larger bed.

Take three measurements first: frame width including side rails, floor to mattress top, and the gap under the frame for the foot of the table. A table is a surface for a laptop, a book or a plate, not a support for standing or transferring. If the table will be used by someone with limited strength or balance, an occupational therapist can advise on setup.

products.name: MAHANCRIS Overbed Table with Wheels
products.description:
The MAHANCRIS is a queen-sized cross-bed desk that stretches 70.9 inches and raises from 36.4 to 43.5 inches in four steps. Its four swivel casters lock, so it can sit beside the bed during use and roll clear when you want the floor space back.

The listing also describes it as converting from a bed table into a standing desk for studying, working or dining. The tradeoff is that the 7 inch height span is modest, and the four fixed levels mean you cannot dial in an in-between setting.

Setup is a matter of attaching the legs and picking a height, then locking all four casters. Compared with the HOOBRO at the same 70.9 inches, the MAHANCRIS has no built-in outlets, so you bring your own power strip, but it does list a clear height range where the YATINEY does not. It suits someone who wants a table that works at the bed and then moves to the chair.
products.bestFor: Queen bed owners who want a clear height range and four locking casters.

products.name: MAHANCRIS Tilt Overbed Table with Shelf
products.description:
This second MAHANCRIS keeps the 70.9 inch length and the 36.4 to 43.5 inch height range, then adds an end stand with 10 tilt angles. When the stand is lifted to its highest setting it can be released so the top lies flat again.

A metal bookshelf, a movable cup holder, a guardrail and four hooks round out the surface, which keeps small essentials close at hand. The tradeoff is that the extra parts, such as the shelf and rail, add weight and give you more pieces to tighten during assembly.

The guardrail helps stop items sliding off a tilted surface, but a laptop still needs a non-slip base if you tilt it steeply. Next to the plain MAHANCRIS, it gives up some uncluttered space for tilt and storage, and next to the LITTLE TREE it offers 10 tilt angles instead of 5. It fits readers and people who keep books, a cup and a few small items on the table.
products.bestFor: Readers and tablet users who want a wide tilt range plus built-in storage.

products.name: HOOBRO Overbed Table with Outlets and Light
products.description:
The HOOBRO has a 70.9 by 15.3 inch top that suits queen beds and smaller, and it integrates a power strip with two standard outlets, one USB port and one Type-C port. A light strip and a drawer are built in, and all four wheels lock.

Height adjusts in four levels, and the listing says it is made of premium particleboard and metal. The tradeoff is that the particleboard top is less forgiving of spills than a wipe-clean surface, and the table is bulky to move and to store.

The drawer is handy for a remote, a charger or reading glasses, but it adds a little weight, so lift from the frame and not the top. Compared with the YATINEY it adds a light and a drawer, and compared with the LITTLE TREE it trades five tilt positions for storage. It is the pick if you want a drawer and a light without paying attention to tilt.
products.bestFor: People who want a drawer, light strip and full power on one queen-sized table.

products.name: YATINEY Overbed Table with Charging Station
products.description:
The YATINEY is described as a minimalist design with no complex adjustable parts, so there are no knobs or levers to loosen over time. Its 70.9 inch desktop holds notebooks, books and a water bottle, and it adds a charging station for devices.

Four caster wheels let it roll between a bed, a sofa and a recliner, though only two of them lock. The tradeoff is that without height steps you accept the one working height, and the listing gives no tilt or capacity numbers to check.

The simple structure is an advantage when the person using it does not want to adjust anything, because the table is either under the bed or it is not. With two locking wheels it parks less firmly than the MAHANCRIS with four, and it lacks the drawer of the HOOBRO. It suits a household that moves the table often and values simplicity.

products.name: TigerDad Heavy Duty Overbed Table
products.description:
The TigerDad's frame telescopes between 55.1 and 82.7 inches, so a queen bed sits near the middle of its range. It lists a 350 lb capacity with a reinforced metal frame and a 15mm E1-grade MDF panel.

The 47.2 by 18.1 inch desktop is deeper than the 15.3 inch HOOBRO, which gives a laptop and a mug more room. The tradeoff is that it has no power strip, light or tilt, so it is a plain surface compared with the powered picks.

Because the length adjusts, it is the easiest to move to another bed or room, and the stated capacity makes it the clearest on loads. Put heavy items near the center rather than at an extended end. If you need power, choose the LITTLE TREE or the HOOBRO instead.

products.name: LITTLE TREE Overbed Table with Outlets
products.description:
The LITTLE TREE pairs a built-in power outlet area, with two AC outlets and two USB ports, with a five-position tabletop that tilts from fully flat. Its legs are height adjustable, and the listing mentions a sliding component as well.

The tilt top lets a book or tablet sit at an angle without a separate stand. The tradeoff is that the listing does not give a length figure in the details, so confirm that it spans your queen frame before ordering.

On setup, plug in the single cord, set the legs and choose a tilt position. It offers fewer tilt angles than the 10 on the tilt MAHANCRIS, but it includes power, which that table lacks. For a table that does both tilt and charging, it is the closest match in the group.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A queen mattress is roughly 60 inches wide, and the table legs need to rest on the floor outside the frame. A top of about 70 inches gives several inches of clearance on each side, which is why the MAHANCRIS, HOOBRO and YATINEY all list 70.9 inches. If your frame has a platform lip, measure its outside edge. A telescoping model such as the TigerDad at 55.1 to 82.7 inches covers wider frames.

The table needs to clear the mattress and the pillow level, then land near your lap. The MAHANCRIS lists 36.4 to 43.5 inches, a 7 inch span, which covers common mattress heights. Measure floor to mattress top and add a few inches for clearance. Fixed steps, as on the HOOBRO's four levels, mean you may not hit an exact height.

A tilting top lifts a book or tablet toward your eyes, but extra moving parts can loosen and steep angles let items slide. The tilt MAHANCRIS offers 10 angles with a guardrail, and the LITTLE TREE offers 5 from fully flat. A non-slip mat or the guardrail on the MAHANCRIS keeps things in place. Choose tilt only if you read or draw on the table daily.

Built-in outlets reduce extension cords, but they tie the table to one wall socket. The HOOBRO provides two AC outlets, USB and Type-C, and the LITTLE TREE gives two AC outlets and two USB ports. Check that the cord reaches the wall from where the table sits. Route the cord so it cannot become a tripping hazard.

Depth decides what fits beside a laptop. The TigerDad Heavy Duty top is 18.1 inches deep, while the HOOBRO is 15.3 inches, and the tilt MAHANCRIS adds a shelf, a cup holder and four hooks. A drawer or shelf keeps small items close, but it uses surface area. Decide whether you want clear space or built-in organization.

Locking wheels keep the table steady when you type or set down a drink. The MAHANCRIS and HOOBRO lock all four, while the YATINEY locks only two of four. Check wheel size and floor type, because small casters struggle on thick carpet. Always lock the brakes before loading weight on the surface.

howWeEvaluated.title: Queen frame fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each table's length against a queen mattress of about 60 inches. The MAHANCRIS, HOOBRO and YATINEY all list 70.9 inches, and the TigerDad adjusts from 55.1 to 82.7 inches. The LITTLE TREE did not list a length, which lowered its score in this category.

howWeEvaluated.title: Adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on product specs, we compared height ranges, steps and tilt angles. The MAHANCRIS lists 36.4 to 43.5 inches, the tilt version adds 10 angles, and the LITTLE TREE offers 5. The YATINEY scores lower because it has no adjusters at all.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted outlets, ports, drawers and shelves. The HOOBRO leads with two AC outlets, USB, Type-C, a drawer and a light strip, while the LITTLE TREE has two AC and two USB. The plain MAHANCRIS and the TigerDad offer no power.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mobility and locking
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at wheel count and how many lock. The MAHANCRIS and HOOBRO lock four wheels, and the YATINEY locks two. Picks with fewer brakes were marked down, since a rolling table is less steady during use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Specification clarity
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on buyer feedback and listings, we rewarded clear numbers. The TigerDad states a 350 lb capacity, and the MAHANCRIS states a height range. Tables with missing lengths or capacities need a seller check before purchase.

faq.q: What length overbed table fits a queen bed?
faq.a: A queen mattress is about 60 inches wide, so a table around 70 inches long gives clearance for the legs on each side. The MAHANCRIS, HOOBRO and YATINEY list 70.9 inches. The TigerDad telescopes from 55.1 to 82.7 inches. Measure the outside of your frame to confirm.

All four is the safest, since a locked table does not creep when you type or rest a plate. The MAHANCRIS and HOOBRO lock four, and the YATINEY locks two of four. Small casters also struggle on thick carpet. Always lock the wheels before you load the surface.

faq.q: Is a tilt top worth it?
faq.a: It is worth it if you read or draw in bed, because it lifts the page toward your eyes. The tilt MAHANCRIS offers 10 angles and the LITTLE TREE offers 5. Tilt tops add parts and steep angles let items slide, so use the guardrail or a mat. If you mostly eat, a flat top is simpler.

faq.q: Can these tables hold a heavy monitor?
faq.a: Only the TigerDad states a capacity, at 350 lb, and the others do not. A listed capacity is for evenly spread weight, not a lever load at one end. Keep heavy items near the center, and confirm with the seller before loading anything heavy.

Not always. The HOOBRO and LITTLE TREE include them, while the MAHANCRIS and TigerDad do not. Outlets reduce cord clutter but tie the table to a wall socket. If you do add a power strip, keep the cord from crossing a walkway.

The HOOBRO uses a particleboard and metal build, and particleboard is less tolerant of spills than a wipe-clean surface. Wipe liquids quickly and use a mat for hot drinks. The TigerDad uses a 15mm E1 MDF panel, which is a similar engineered wood. A mat helps protect any wood-based top.

faq.q: Can I use it as a standing desk?
faq.a: The MAHANCRIS listing describes converting to a standing desk, with a height range up to 43.5 inches. Whether that suits you depends on your height, and an overbed table is not a support aid. Do not lean on it for balance. Check that the wheels are locked when standing at it.
